record.original_question: Let E be the compact plane set of transfinite diameter (=capacity) d(E) = 1 and let Y dn (E)n(n−1)/2 = max |wµ − wν |. wν ∈E 1≤µ<ν≤n It is known that dn (E) decreases with n and dn (E) → d(E) as n → ∞, so that dn (E) ≥ 1 is trivial. It is known by Pommerenke [648], that dn (E) ≥ n2/(n−1) if E is connected. Is this inequality true in general? Further, is it true that dn (E)(n−1)/2 ≤ Kn if E is connected, where K is some absolute constant? It is known that 4  dn (E)(n−1)/2 ≤ log n + 4 n, e in this case. (Ch. Pommerenke)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ be a compact set with logarithmic capacity (transfinite diameter) $d(E)=1$. For each integer $n\ge 2$, define the $n$-th diameter $d_n(E)$ by
$$d_n(E)^{n(n-1)/2} \;=\; \max_{w_1,\ldots,w_n\in E}\;\prod_{1\le \mu<\nu\le n}|w_\mu-w_\nu|.$$
It is classical that $d_n(E)$ is non-increasing in $n$ and $d_n(E)\to d(E)=1$, so $d_n(E)\ge 1$. Pommerenke proved that if $E$ is connected, then 
$$d_n(E)\;\ge\; n^{1/(n-1)}\quad\text{(equivalently, }d_n(E)^{n-1}\ge n\text{).}$$

(a) Does the inequality $d_n(E)\ge n^{1/(n-1)}$ hold for every compact set $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ with $d(E)=1$, without the assumption of connectedness?

(b) Does there exist an absolute constant $K>0$ such that, for every connected compact set $E\subset\mathbb{C}$ with $d(E)=1$ and every $n\ge 2$,
$$d_n(E)^{(n-1)/2}\;\le\; K\,n\,?$$
(For connected $E$ it is known that $d_n(E)^{(n-1)/2}\le\bigl(\tfrac{4}{e}\log n+4\bigr)n$.)
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a definitive resolution of either question. The lower bound $d_n(E)\ge n^{1/(n-1)}$ for general (not necessarily connected) compact plane sets of capacity 1, and the conjectured sharp linear-in-$n$ upper bound for $d_n(E)^{(n-1)/2}$ in the connected case (improving the known $(\tfrac{4}{e}\log n+4)n$ bound), do not appear to have been established in the literature surveyed.
